paper.title: A New Product Growth for Model Consumer Durables

headline: Bass 1969 (agent-based): 2/3 locked clauses REPRO; measured discrete peak tick = 8 vs continuous t* = 6.19 (offset +29%), final adoption 0.993

verdicts.gate: P1 cumulative adoption is a sigmoid reaching near-full adoption
P2 measured peak-adoption tick within +-15% of continuous t*=ln(q/p)/(p+q)
reasons: measured discrete peak tick = 8 vs continuous t* = 6.1926: offset +29.2% (need within +-15%). Discrete-vs-continuous subtlety: the unit-Δt Bass map lags the continuous ODE peak (forward-difference lag)

verdicts.gate: P3 q>p => interior bell peak; q=0 => rate monotonically decreasing

extra.discrete_vs_continuous_note: the agent model advances in unit-Δt ticks; the analytic t* is a continuous-time result. The discrete Bass map (forward-difference) systematically lags the continuous ODE peak, so the measured peak tick sits later than t*. This is a known discretization effect, not an artifact — verified: the deterministic mean-field discrete map peaks at the same tick as the stochastic agent runs.
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the Bass S-curve / bell-rate result and would catch an artifact

citations: Bass, F.M. (1969). A New Product Growth for Model Consumer Durables. Management Science 15(5):215-227. doi:10.1287/mnsc.15.5.215.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction
